turns.content: At equal pressure and temperature, gas Y has density 0.39 times that of carbon dioxide and is basic. Calculate its molar mass and identify the most plausible gas.

One mole of a binary metal-nonmetal compound A reacts with excess water to form 2 mol of Y and 3 mol of a sparingly soluble base Z. Infer the formula type of A and write the balanced hydrolysis pattern.
Using that formula type, calculate the metal's relative atomic mass from the 18:7 metal-to-nonmetal mass ratio.
Identify the metal and check it against the flame-test observation and the limited water solubility of Z.
Calculate the molar mass of A and place it in the corresponding 20 g/mol-wide interval.
Check the identification independently against all quantitative and qualitative constraints established in the preceding steps.
Report Y, Z, and A, together with the molar mass and its interval.
